The raw_customers table is an SCD2-style dimension. It has 230 rows for 200 distinct customers: 200 rows with is_current=True and 30 historical rows with is_current=False. silver_customers keeps all 230 rows, so the join fans out for the 30 customers that have history. That explains why gold_region_daily counts more than silver_transactions (5415 vs 4699).

The fix is to keep only current rows in silver_customers. There are exactly 200 current rows for 200 distinct customers, so each customer has one current row.

The historical rows have valid_from 2023-06-01 and the current rows 2025-01-01. All transactions fall in January 2026, after both dates. The current row is therefore the correct version for every transaction, and no point-in-time join is needed.

The check on counts: 5415 − 4699 = 716 extra rows, which is plausible for 30 of 200 customers with an extra row each (about 15% of 4699 is about 705).

The fix filters on is_current in silver_customers. The other gold tables are unaffected.
